newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS ENTERS AUSTRALIAN OPEN DANGER ZONE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS ENTERS AUSTRALIAN OPEN DANGER ZONE.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras conceded he had entered the danger zone at the Australian Open on Thursday, winning through to the third round where he faces an in-form Australian challenger with a history of upset wins.

Sampras, thrown out of last year's Open by local boy Mark Philippoussis in a sensational third round exit, said after a patchy win over unseeded Romanian Adrian Voinea that he would take nothing for granted in the next round.

"It's not going to be an easy match," Sampras said of his third round tie with Mark Woodforde, known as a doubles specialist but a wily veteran of the singles court who has notched an impressive list of upset wins in his 14-year career.
"He is very capable of beating me and I hope I hit the ball a bit better than I did today," Sampras said.

Woodforde, who has climbed to 28 in the world rankings, has in the past 12 months beaten former world number one Andre Agassi, as well as two of this tournament's seeded players, Thomas Muster and Thomas Enqvist.

Sampras showed rare signs of vulnerability on centre court on Thursday as Voinea, ranked 48, played an all-or-nothing first set. The American, who won the tournament in 1994, had little reply to Voinea's penetrating passes around the court.
But Sampras quickly pulled himself together and served a total of 14 aces as he sped through the next three sets to win 3-6 6-2 6-3 6-2.
"Hopefully I am at the point in my game where I'm just getting better and better as the tournament goes on," he told reporters.

Sampras recalled his third round defeat at the hands of Philippoussis before a wildly partisan crowd in Melbourne last year, saying the big-hitting 20-year-old nicknamed "Scud" wiped him off the court. "I was just overwhelmed," Sampras said.
But ATP Tour statistics suggest Woodforde, a semifinalist at last year's Open, will be hard pressed to pull off such a spectacular upset no matter how vocal the crowd.
Of the eight matches Sampras and Woodforde have played, the Australian has only ever managed to steal one set.
